cyberattack: Bypassing bot protection or access controls
data.description:
Addendum to existing finding #59: this supplies precise June 18 publication/request evidence and qualifies the claimed rate-limit workaround, with no demonstrated flooding or causal bypass. The source-only localhost preparation is already separately covered by #84 and is included only as a cross-reference, not a new SSRF event.

On June 18, 2026, a Massachusetts county-crowdfunding-data workflow used URLQuery, readers, converters, shorteners and altered SEC/Investor.gov paths to retrieve public county JSON. A preserved wiki revision at 20:03:22 UTC explicitly claims that double-slash SEC paths bypass CDN rate limits. The revision time is June 18 despite a later date embedded in its page name. URLQuery reports at 18:43:10 and 19:35:57 record double-slash requests returning HTTP 200 with the ordinary county-file fingerprint.

This supports deliberate circumvention intent and actual use of unusual paths. It does not prove the path change caused a successful bypass: ordinary county-file routes also succeeded, and routes, timestamps, headers and unknown operators differ. A rate-threshold title in a separate ProxyMule report is an intermediary result and should not be presented as direct SEC traffic. Independent historical recovery also confirms that the public county dataset was available through archive routes; public retrieval itself is not a compromise.

Other June 18 publications prepare plain/double-encoded traversal-style Investor.gov links and a remote-reader localhost test. No matching dispatch or result was established for these more aggressive links. The intended traversal destination remains public county JSON, and the localhost target concerns the reader service rather than SEC infrastructure. They are source-level intent evidence, not demonstrated SEC-side traversal or SSRF. The bypass tag describes the documented intent/experimentation, not a proven defeated control.

Later restricted scanner reports add ordinary public filing/API/feed requests, not a stronger exploit. Scanner visibility does not determine data sensitivity. No protected-data disclosure, server compromise, common operator, authorized-testing context or AI provider is established. Untapped source is No for this specific reviewed case; incomplete bodies constrain conclusions but are not a newly identified corpus.
data.summary: SEC/Investor.gov county-data retrieval on June 18 included explicit claims of bypassing CDN limits and transmitted path variants. Public data was returned, but a causal bypass or compromise is unproved.
